background_notes.fact: For a continuous path u on a compact interval which is continuously differentiable on each member of a finite partition, with values in a Sobolev Hilbert space, u(t)-u(a)=integral_a^t u'(s) ds. For an integrable Hilbert-valued path F, ||integral_J F||<=integral_J ||F||. A bounded linear operator commutes with this integral. These assertions apply to the smooth spatial paths and continuous piecewise smooth time paths here; identities can be established on each smooth segment and summed.

background_notes.justification: The fundamental theorem for a continuously differentiable Hilbert-valued path follows by integrating its derivative on each smooth piece; continuity cancels adjacent endpoint values. The integral norm inequality follows first for step functions by the triangle inequality and then by integral approximation. Bounded linear maps pass through the same approximation. The compact interval meets only finitely many steps since tau>0. These facts justify integration of the error equation, projection of integrals, and summation across step endpoints without any exchange of a singular limit.

background_notes.justification: Deleting terms contracts a nonnegative weighted Fourier sum. On |k|>N, (1+k^2)^(-1/2)<=N^(-1); on |k|<=N, k^2<=N^2; on |k|>N/3, (1+k^2)^(-pstar/2)<=3^pstar N^(-pstar). These give the three inequalities by squaring and summing. Fixed bounded Fourier projections commute with weak time derivatives, and restricting a supremum or essential supremum cannot increase it. Each low input has finite Fourier support |k|<=N/3, and multiplication adds indices; neither P, S nor Dinv adds indices. Thus the all-low trilinear integrand and its time integral have support |k|<=N. This is precisely the routine Fourier content used in S002-S004.
